readings: Treating a rental_duration of 5 days or more (rental_duration >= 5) as a long rental period, look only at the long-rental films and group them by `rating`. For each rating, show the rating, the average per film of `rental_rate` divided by `rental_duration` (ignoring missing values), the number of films, and that average divided by an overall benchmark. The benchmark is the plain unweighted mean of the per-rating averages across all ratings in this long-rental set, ignoring any missing ones. If the benchmark itself is missing, return no rows. Leave all values unrounded.

Treating a rental_duration of more than 5 days (rental_duration > 5, so 5 days itself is not long) as a long rental period, look only at the long-rental films and group them by `rating`. For each rating, show the rating, the average per film of `rental_rate` divided by `rental_duration` (ignoring missing values), the number of films, and that average divided by an overall benchmark. The benchmark is the plain unweighted mean of the per-rating averages across all ratings in this long-rental set, ignoring any missing ones. If the benchmark itself is missing, return no rows. Leave all values unrounded.
queries:
WITH per_rating AS (
  SELECT rating,
         AVG(rental_rate * 1.0 / rental_duration) AS avg_ratio,
         COUNT(*) AS film_count
  FROM film
  WHERE rental_duration >= 5
  GROUP BY rating
),
benchmark AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS bench
  FROM per_rating
  WHERE avg_ratio IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT p.rating,
       p.avg_ratio,
       p.film_count,
       p.avg_ratio / b.bench AS ratio_to_benchmark
FROM per_rating p
CROSS JOIN benchmark b
WHERE b.bench IS NOT NULL;
WITH r AS (
  SELECT rating,
         AVG(rental_rate * 1.0 / rental_duration) AS avg_ratio,
         COUNT(*) AS film_count
  FROM film
  WHERE rental_duration > 5
  GROUP BY rating
),
b AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS benchmark FROM r
)
SELECT r.rating,
       r.avg_ratio,
       r.film_count,
       r.avg_ratio / b.benchmark
FROM r, b
WHERE b.benchmark IS NOT NULL;
